documents.title: SGD to IDR payout incident postmortem
documents.content_markdown:
# SGD to IDR payout incident postmortem

Fictional hackathon data for Company A. This is not a real incident or a real company record.

Incident reference: INC-2026-0814. Owner: Aisha Lim, incident commander.

## Summary

On 14 August 2026, the SGD to IDR payout corridor was disrupted from 09:10 to 14:10 Singapore time. All affected items were reconciled by 14:10.

A downstream payout partner changed its request contract and began requiring the field `destination_branch_code`. Company A's corridor validation did not reject requests when that field was blank. The partner rejected those requests.

## Retry behavior

The retry worker queued 12 additional jobs for payouts that were already in the queue. The incident team cancelled those duplicate jobs before settlement. No duplicate beneficiary payments were completed. Duplicate queue entries and duplicate settled payments are different outcomes.

## Recovery

At 09:10 the team paused the affected corridor. Engineers added a temporary validation check and corrected the invalid payloads. Operations replayed each approved payout once after reconciliation checks. At 14:10 reconciliation completed and the corridor resumed.

## Follow-up work

PAY-101 adds permanent validation for the partner's required field.
PAY-102 adds an idempotency guard to the retry worker.
PAY-103 adds alerts for unusual rejection rates in this corridor.

Current ticket statuses and closure times belong to the Jira records. Approval evidence belongs to the Slack sign-off thread. The current operating procedure is the payout runbook.

## Diagnostic reference

The diagnostic correlation key recorded in this postmortem is `IDR-VAL-714`. This reference is deliberately unique to this document for the permission-revocation test.

Customer counts, payout amounts, and reporting decisions are maintained separately by Compliance.

documents.title: SGD to IDR payout recovery runbook
documents.content_markdown:
# SGD to IDR payout recovery runbook

Fictional hackathon data for Company A. This is not a real incident or a real company record.

Runbook reference: RB-IDR-01. Owner: Payments Engineering.
This is version 1 of the demo runbook.

## Recovery procedure

1. Pause dispatch for the affected corridor and identify the affected payout IDs.
2. Confirm each payout includes a non-empty `destination_branch_code` that matches the partner contract.
3. Check the retry idempotency key for each payout. Cancel duplicate queued jobs before replay.
4. Confirm reconciliation status with the incident commander and replay each approved payout once.
5. Compare dispatch and settlement records before returning the corridor to normal operation.

## Change record

On 20 August, the runbook incorporated the permanent validator from PAY-101 and the retry idempotency guard from PAY-102. The linked Slack sign-off thread records who approved each change. PAY-103 remains a separate monitoring improvement.

This runbook does not contain customer impact figures or regulatory filing decisions.

# PAY-102 Prevent duplicate queued retries

Fictional hackathon data for Company A. This is not a real incident or a real company record.

Status: Done
Owner: Ben Ho
Created: 14 August 2026 at 15:10 Singapore time
Closed: 20 August 2026 at 16:30 Singapore time
Related incident: INC-2026-0814

## Work completed

The retry worker checks a stable payout idempotency key before inserting another queued job. A repeated request with the same key does not create an additional active job.

## Acceptance evidence

The test cases cover repeated requests and two workers attempting the same payout concurrently. Both cases retain one active queued job.

Ravi Shah approved the change in the Slack sign-off thread on 20 August at 16:00. The ticket was then moved to Done at 16:30. The runbook includes the duplicate-job check.

This work addresses duplicate queue entries. It does not imply that duplicate payments settled during the incident.

documents.title: SG entity incident assessment and demo filing record
documents.content_markdown:
# SG entity incident assessment and demo filing record

Fictional hackathon data for Company A. This is not a real incident or a real company record.

Record: COMP-INC-2026-0814
Owner: Priya Menon
Entity: SG demo entity
Related incident: INC-2026-0814

## Incident assessment

On 14 August 2026, the SGD to IDR payout service was disrupted from 09:10 to 14:10 Singapore time. The impact register records 340 affected payouts across 280 unique customers.

Of these, 300 payouts were held before debit. Another 40 payouts, involving 32 customers, had been debited while beneficiary credit was pending. The temporarily unsettled debited amount was SGD 42,000 equivalent. All affected payouts were reconciled by 14:10, with no principal loss recorded in this exercise.

## Reporting decision under the fictional exercise policy

The exercise assumes the SG demo entity must submit a notification by 17 August 2026 at 17:00 Singapore time. This is an invented deadline for the demonstration, not a statement of any regulator's requirements.

The simulated filing was submitted on 17 August at 15:20 Singapore time, before that deadline. Its internal receipt reference is DEMO-SG-0817-1520.

The Indonesian demo payout partner was notified on 14 August at 10:00 Singapore time. The exercise does not determine a separate Indonesian regulatory filing obligation. No EU-entity records are included or assessed.

## Evidence

The impact register supplies the counts and amounts. The reconciliation and communications record confirms resolution. Engineering implementation details are outside this record.
